topSignals.title: Project Jupiter's Dec 7 air-quality permit hearing vacated — no new date set.
topSignals.text: New Mexico hearing officer James Browning vacated the opening of the contested-case hearing on the air-quality permit for Oracle/Yucca Growth Infrastructure's Bloom Energy SOFC fuel-cell microgrid serving the Santa Teresa ("Project Jupiter") data center, after the state Environment Department and the developer jointly asked (Nov 3) for more time to technically review October's power-plan revisions and issue public notices. No replacement hearing date was set; regular scheduling conferences were ordered instead, and the previous Nov 23 permit-decision deadline was waived. New Energy Economy's renewed motion to dismiss the application was again denied — Browning said he lacks the technical evidence or authority to grant it — and a state motion for expert-witness disclosure requirements was also denied. Oracle said it "look[s] forward to moving efficiently toward a hearing date and schedule." This is a new procedural delay (reported Nov 6), on top of — not instead of — the prior case history (NM Supreme Court stay lifted in September, dismissal-motion-rejected/hearing-confirmed in late October); it does not affect Bloom Energy installation progress at the site, only the regulatory permit timeline. Albuquerque Journal

Competitor roster: SOFC systems for data centers

Bloom Energy: Deployed/signed at multiple named sites — Oracle/Project Jupiter (NM, installation underway; Dec 7 air-permit hearing vacated Nov 6, no new date set), AEP (1 GW), Brookfield EaaS, Nebius (328 MW/$2.6B, Vineland NJ), Equinix (>100 MW/19 sites), Aligned "Project Phoenix" (2 GW, PA), Hitachi (Japan), SK Eternix (Icheon/Paju, Korea, 28 MW, operational).

FuelCell Energy (incl. HyAxiom-branded products): Signed orders/PPAs — Fit Energy (up to 380 MW), Inuverse Korea (up to 100 MW), 75 MW Texas Capacity Reservation Agreement, SDCL (up to 450 MW). No named deployment live yet.

Doosan Fuel Cell/HyAxiom: Signed order — US AI data center supply contract (KRW 823.6B cumulative, mixed SOFC/PAFC); separately supplies SOFC stacks to Reverion. No named data-center site of its own yet.
Convion: Pipeline-only/pre-commercial under HD Hyundai ownership; no named data-center customer.
SK ecoplant: Pipeline-only (2023-vintage GDS Singapore SOFC deal); no new named data-center deployment.
Ceres Power's SOFC licensees (Doosan, Delta Electronics, Weichai): Licensing/pipeline-only; no named data-center deployment via Ceres licensing directly.
Reverion: Pipeline-only — Doosan-supplied SOFC stacks for rSOC power plants (Germany); no named data-center customer yet.
Petra Power: Pre-commercial, no named customer; first infrastructure deployment targeted 2028.
